items.title: Vince DiMartino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 8, 2025
items.q: I like Haydn’s Concerto but I think Joe Smith, you know, I like the way he plays it better.

ctx.x: I don’t know that sounds fishy to me.

It is. And you know it was great because I felt like that was a good function for — and I bought some records occasionally you know and stuff like that. But mostly I used it to feel like I was helping with the family stuff you know. And I think that’s a good — and I tell students this all the time. I say, “Look, the most important thing is to be an asset to your community.” I say “It doesn’t matter if you’re on Carnegie Hall stage that’s a community. Make sure you’re doing what is necessary to be an asset to that…

Yeah. You know you made me think about when I look at your resume and your list of accomplishments and things you’ve done, I wonder if there’s a difference in your mindset in your preparation and your whole demeanor from playing — I know a mutual friend mentioned that you had played “A Soldier’s Tale” — a Stravinsky.
